title: Hybrid heuristic + forecasting autoscaler with per-tenant safety envelope
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Dedicated customers need predictable throughput and cost controls. Current autoscaler reacts to short-term signals (utilization, queue length) but can overprovision during sudden bursts and underprovision for predictable daily patterns. We need a hybrid autoscaling engine that combines fast heuristic controllers for immediate latency SLOs with short-horizon demand forecasts to pre-scale safely, plus per-tenant safety envelopes to enforce throughput guarantees and cost caps.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler triggers scale-up within 30s for synthetic p95 latency breach in 95% of test runs
Forecast component improves 60m ahead throughput error (MAPE) by >=25% vs baseline naive average
Per-tenant safety envelope prevents scaling beyond max_nodes and enforces minimum reserved capacity
New autoscaler exposes metrics: forecasted_tokens_per_min, scale_reason_tags, and safety_block_events
End-to-end tests in staging demonstrate no regressions on cold-start latency and CPU/GPU utilization remains within expected bounds
decision_log: 2025-11-11: Picked hybrid design - combine PID-like heuristic for immediate response + XGBoost forecasting for 5-60m horizon. Rationale: heuristics handle microbursts, model handles diurnal patterns.
2025-11-13: Safety envelope will be first-class per-tenant config: min_reserved, max_allowed, surge_budget, cooldown_window. Defaults are conservative to avoid cost surprises.
2025-11-15: Use token-level throughput (tokens/min) and p95 generation latency as primary target metrics. Secondary signals: queue_depth, GPU_utilization, KV_cache_hit_rate.
2025-11-17: Rollout plan uses canary by tenant tier: start with internal tenants, then enterprise alpha customers, then 10% of production traffic via weighted routing.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Add forecast service prototype (batch training + streaming inference) that emits tokens_per_min predictions per tenant. Store predictions in time-series DB (Prometheus/tempo annotation).
Week 2: Implement heuristic controller module (PID-ish) inside autoscaler runtime. Expose scale decisions with reason tags and confidence score.
Week 3: Implement safety envelope enforcement layer that vetoes scaler decisions and suggests alternatives (eg. temporary model degradation to cheaper variant).
Week 4: Integration tests + load tests. Add feature flags to toggle forecasting and safety enforcement per-tenant.
Week 5: Staged rollout to internal, evaluate metrics, iterate thresholds.
Code touches: autoscaler service (runtime), forecasting service (new microservice), console UI for safety envelopes, API schema updates for tenant config.
test_plan: Unit tests for forecast model serialization and prediction consumption
Chaos tests simulating sudden 10x burst and verifying heuristic fast-path scales within target window
Backtest forecasts on 90 days of historical telemetry for top 50 tenants; compute MAPE and tail errors
Integration tests with dedicated pool simulator to assert min_reserved and max_allowed constraints
A/B comparison in staging: current autoscaler vs hybrid for cost-per-token and p95 latency over 48h
rollout_plan: Enable forecast for internal tenants only and run in shadow mode for 3 days
Enable safety_envelope for internal tenants and test veto flow with synthetic bursts
Canary: enable for enterprise-alpha tenants (n=5) for 1 week
Gradual ramp: +10% tenants every 48h with monitoring guardrails, automatic rollback on incident
risks_and_mitigation: Forecast inaccuracy -> risk of pre-scaling unnecessarily. Mitigation: conservative scaling multiplier, cap by surge_budget, require cross-signal agreement before pre-scale.
Safety envelope too restrictive -> may cause SLO violations. Mitigation: automated telemetry that warns when min_reserved is insufficient; allow emergency override with audit log.
Model/drift operational complexity -> risk of hidden failures. Mitigation: model health checks, shadow runs, and fallbacks to pure heuristic if model fails.
Cost spike during rollout -> mitigation: billing alerting and per-tenant cost caps during canary
